title: Owl At Home
author: Arnold Lobel

hero.name: Owl
hero.description: A friendly brown owl who lives in a cozy home, wears no clothes, main character of Arnold Lobel's easy reader
hero.source_note: Generic owl symbol from Boardmaker should suffice; if a more Lobel-specific illustration is desired, source from TPT or Creative Fabrica

ambiguous.issue: Could mean a destructive fire or a cozy fireplace fire
ambiguous.reason: In the book Owl sits by a warm fire in his fireplace; the cozy hearth meaning is correct

ambiguous.issue: Could mean a teardrop (crying) or to tear/rip something
ambiguous.reason: In the story 'Tear-Water Tea', Owl collects sad tears to make tea; the crying/teardrop noun meaning is correct

notes: Owl At Home by Arnold Lobel is a classic easy reader with five gentle chapters. Key recurring themes are Owl's cozy home, the changing seasons/winter weather, night-time, the moon, and emotional moments like tear-water tea. The word 'tear' should map to a teardrop/crying image. 'Fire' should map to a fireplace rather than a destructive fire. Owl is a generic animal that Boardmaker covers well, so no special sourcing is needed for the hero unless the teacher wants a Lobel-style illustration.

matching.note: Min 4 approved stems, no hard cap

cvc_decode.note: 3-5 groups x 3 CVC words (phonics, not theme icons)
